rationale: All three blocking findings are resolved. CR-001 (security — verbatim headers in checkpoint): _SENSITIVE_HEADER_NAMES frozenset added at module level covering the 6 most common credential-bearing headers; dict comprehension with k.lower() normalization filters before injection; guard 'if safe_headers:' ensures the key is absent when all headers are redacted — satisfies the minimum denylist approach recommended by the finding. CR-002 (empty-dict test gap): test parametrized @pytest.mark.parametrize('headers', [None, {}]), both falsy paths now exercised. CR-003 (by-reference mutation): dict comprehension creates a new dict object, eliminating reference sharing with self.request_headers. No new high-risk issues detected in the fix-up diff. The lambda→named-function refactoring visible in workflow.py hunk (lines 734-383) is a pre-existing branch change unrelated to EPMCDME-11692 and does not introduce new risk. Narrow confirmation pass not dispatched — fixes are simple, direct, and clearly address each concern.
